purpose: Hourly authoritative-vendor research delta. Evidence upgrades remain spec-level only; no tenant credentials were used and connector writes remain disabled.

patch.evidenceNote: IFS Cloud officially exposes REST APIs using OData, with OpenAPI v2/v3 specifications available from API Explorer. Premium and Integration APIs are preferred for system integrations; Entity Service APIs can expose entity models for CRUD/state transitions but require administrator activation. Projection permission sets support read-only access, which is the required WFM starting posture. No tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: OAuth 2.0 identity scoped to required API projections
read-only projection permission sets wherever available
no Entity Service mutation permissions during discovery
dataAvailableOrExpected: tenant-exposed OData entity sets and projection data
ERP/manufacturing entity data exposed by authorised Premium, Integration or Entity Service APIs
automationOpportunities: production-demand refresh from authorised ERP projections
approved labour/cost export only after write-roundtrip certification
customerValue: faster ERP integration through published OData/OpenAPI contracts
savingsHypotheses: reduce manual finance and production-data reconciliation
reduce implementation effort by reusing stable published projections
reduce overstaffing when production demand can be read from IFS
dataGaps: exact enabled projections and manufacturing objects are tenant/version specific
constraintsRisks: Entity Service APIs require administrator activation
deprecated API versions must not be selected for new adapters
write-capable entity services remain disabled in WFM

patch.evidenceNote: Epicor documents Kinetic Open REST API as platform-level access to ERP services, data and business logic. The API is OData v4-compliant, versioned, discoverable through built-in REST help, and protected by API keys, access scopes and ERP user/data permissions. This provides a usable route for manufacturing orders, resources, costs and related ERP context once a customer tenant is authorised. No tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: API key restricted by access scope
ERP user/data permissions limited to required read services
no business-logic execution permission during discovery unless separately required
dataAvailableOrExpected: manufacturing/order/resource/cost context exposed by the customer's enabled ERP services
automationOpportunities: production/order changes can trigger labour-plan recalculation once representative reads are proven
approved labour/cost feedback can be considered only after controlled write certification
customerValue: faster implementation through OData-compatible service discovery
savingsHypotheses: identify labour variance against manufacturing demand
reduce planning latency between ERP order changes and workforce schedules
dataGaps: available business objects and customisations vary by Kinetic tenant/version
resource and labour semantics require canonical mapping validation
constraintsRisks: API key access must also be constrained by Epicor access scopes and ERP permissions
service versions and customer customisations require compatibility testing

patch.evidenceNote: Ignition 8.3 documents a dynamically generated OpenAPI/REST interface at /openapi and /openapi.json, OPC UA client/server connectivity, and Edge IIoT MQTT publication. HTTP API tokens can reach mutative routes and vendor guidance warns they can modify configuration, tags or projects, so WFM must use a segregated read-only facade or equivalent gateway controls rather than assuming a token alone is least privilege. No plant or tenant connection was attempted.

requiredPermissions: read-only tag/telemetry access through a segregated facade or equivalent policy boundary
OPC UA/MQTT subscription rights limited to required namespaces/topics
dataAvailableOrExpected: industrial tags and machine/process state made available through OPC UA
Gateway API metadata exposed through documented OpenAPI routes
automationOpportunities: machine-stop events can trigger labour redeployment recommendations
machine restart/recovery can trigger staffing recall recommendations
correlate staffed time with machine state and output evidence
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time during equipment stops
reduce labour waiting for unavailable machines
quantify labour cost of downtime by shift/work centre
dataGaps: tag names and semantics are site-specific
machine output/OEE meaning requires customer asset mapping
timestamps and historian retention require site validation
constraintsRisks: Ignition API tokens may reach mutative HTTP API routes
plant-network connectivity must terminate at a controlled site-edge boundary
WFM must not issue PLC/tag writes or control methods by default

systems.name: Siemens Industrial Edge
systems.evidenceNote: Siemens documents public Industrial Edge management APIs, token-based IEM access, and an IE Device Kit based on gRPC/Protocol Buffers; the fabric reuses its existing Protobuf RPC/HTTP2 profile rather than creating a duplicate transport. Industrial Edge also supports shop-floor connectivity through MQTT and OPC UA. Device Kit 1.29.0 (06/2026) added an API-only external-endpoint TCP connectivity check useful for preflight validation. WFM should consume telemetry/health read-only; device onboarding, app deployment and industrial-control actions remain separately gated. No tenant or edge-device authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: time-limited Industrial Edge token scoped to required read endpoints
no device onboarding, application deployment or industrial-control permissions
dataAvailableOrExpected: edge/device and connectivity metadata exposed through documented APIs
shop-floor telemetry routed through MQTT/OPC UA integrations
external-endpoint connectivity status useful for integration preflight
automationOpportunities: preflight plant endpoint reachability before enabling a connector
machine/connectivity state can trigger workforce disruption workflows
reuse customer edge routing instead of creating direct cloud-to-PLC connectivity
customerValue: reuse of existing Siemens edge investment
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time by reacting to machine/connectivity loss
avoid additional bespoke plant gateways where Industrial Edge already provides the approved boundary
dataGaps: exact telemetry objects depend on deployed Industrial Edge apps and plant mappings
customer network segmentation and edge policies determine reachable assets
constraintsRisks: management-plane APIs can change device/application state and remain outside normal WFM authority
industrial-control writes are prohibited by default
short-lived access tokens require secure rotation without broadening scopes
